issues.description: Transform callable is silently ignored when delimiter is used
issues.detail: The new split happens before the existing transform loop further down in get_param_as_list, but more importantly the invariant for the function — 'each returned element has been passed through transform' — is preserved only because the surrounding code still iterates. However, the diff shows only the split; reviewers should confirm that when delimiter is supplied with transform=int (for example), the resulting tokens go through transform. The added tests do not cover delimiter combined with transform, leaving the contract under-audited. Add a test like get_param_as_list('xs', delimiter='|', transform=int) to lock the invariant.

issues.description: Interaction with keep_blank_qs_values is asserted in docs but not tested
issues.detail: The new docstring explicitly states that keep_blank_qs_values 'has no effect on the secondary splitting by delimiter'. That is a behavioral claim about an invariant — a value like 'a||b' under delimiter='|' will yield ['a', '', 'b'] regardless of the option. Such a claim deserves a proof-by-test. Without it, the documented invariant is unverified and easy to regress.

issues.description: Delimiter validation rejects legitimate single-character delimiters like ';' or '\t'
issues.detail: _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS is a closed set of five entries. A caller passing delimiter=';' gets ValueError, which the test even codifies. The data-structure choice — a fixed dict acting as both validator and alias map — conflates two concerns: (a) translating OpenAPI symbolic names to characters, and (b) restricting which characters are allowed. A cleaner factoring is a small alias dict (pipeDelimited->|, spaceDelimited->' ') plus a rule like 'must be a single character'. That keeps the OpenAPI convenience without forbidding semicolons in user code. Worth flagging as a design choice rather than a bug.

issues.description: Default for delimiter inconsistent between overloads and implementation
issues.detail: All six @overload signatures declare 'delimiter: str | None = None' as a concrete default, but overload defaults should conventionally be '= ...' (Ellipsis) to indicate 'see the implementation'. Mixing '= None' into overloads is harmless at runtime but is a small literate-programming smell: the overloads now overstate what they specify. Aligning them to '= ...' matches the surrounding style (store: StoreArg = ..., default: list[str] | None = ...).

issues.description: Complexity and allocation are fine but worth stating
issues.detail: The added work is one dict lookup plus a single str.split — O(n) in the value length, one allocation for the resulting list. No hidden quadratic, no regex. The function reads correctly and terminates trivially (str.split always terminates). No optimization is warranted here; this is the 97% where premature optimization would be wrong. Calling it out so the rigor is explicit rather than implied.

review.summary: The change is small, well-scoped, and reads cleanly: a dict maps OpenAPI symbolic delimiter names to characters, and a single str.split is performed when the parameter arrived as a lone string. Algorithmically it is RIGOROUS — O(n) in the value length, one allocation, obvious termination — and the documented invariant (no split when the parameter is already a list) is preserved by the isinstance(items, str) guard. The audit gaps are in coverage, not correctness: the interaction with transform=... and with keep_blank_qs_values is asserted in prose but not proved by test. The fixed validator dict also doubles as an allow-list that forbids reasonable single-character delimiters like ';', which is a design choice worth a second look rather than a defect. Overall UNDER-AUDITED on the test side; the implementation itself is sound.
